## aws-docs

    # AWS Documentation MCP Server

    This server provides tools to access public AWS documentation, search for content, and get recommendations.

    ## Best Practices

    - For long documentation pages, make multiple calls to `read_documentation` with different `start_index` values for pagination
    - By default, use read_sections when the answer could be within a specific section(s), given the table of contents. Otherwise, use read_documentation to scan the entire page.
    - For very long documents (>30,000 characters), stop reading if you've found the needed information
    - When searching, use specific technical terms rather than general phrases
    - Use `recommend` tool to discover related content that might not appear in search results
    - For recent updates to a service, get an URL for any page in that service, then check the **New** section of the `recommend` tool output on that URL
    - If multiple searches with similar terms yield insufficient results, pivot to using `recommend` to find related pages.
    - Always cite the documentation URL when providing information to users

    ## Tool Selection Guide

    - Use `search_documentation` when: You need to find documentation about a specific AWS service or feature
    - Use `read_documentation` when: You have a specific documentation URL and need its content
    - Use `read_sections` when: You have a specific documentation URL and specific section title(s) and want content from those specific section(s)
    - Use `recommend` when: You want to find related content to a documentation page you're already viewing or need to find newly released information
    - Use `recommend` as a fallback when: Multiple searches have not yielded the specific information needed

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. 7	Hallazgos confirmados al levantar OpenFang v0.5.9 en VM Rocky Linux 9 (apps/ai/):
8	
9	1. **Imagen `ghcr.io/RightNow-AI/openfang:0.5.9` NO es pública** — retorna `unauthorized` al `docker pull`. El propio `docker-compose.yml` del repo lo dice ("GHCR image is not yet public, build from source"). Workaround: clonar repo + `docker build`. Issue tracker: https://github.com/RightNow-AI/openfang/issues/12
10	
11	2. **Build Rust release en e2-medium (2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM) toma ~80 minutos** con `--build-arg LTO=false --build-arg CODEGEN_UNITS=16`. Imagen final pesa 1.74 GB (Rust + python3 + nodejs + wasmtime con todos los features). Sin esos build args (LTO=true, CODEGEN_UNITS=1) probablemente OOM. Para CI/CD futuro: usar machine más grande o pre-built image en AR Liftit.
12	
13	3. **OpenFang busca config en `~/.openfang/config.toml`** (= `/root/.openfang/config.toml` cuando container corre como root). `OPENFANG_HOME=/data` (env del Dockerfile) es para el **data store** (sqlite, workspaces, daemon.json) — NO para config. Si montas config en `/data/.openfang/config.toml` se ignora silenciosamente.
14	
15	4. **OpenFang autodetecta el provider LLM por env vars** — escoge basado en cuál de `{OPENROUTER,ANTHROPIC,OPENAI,GROQ}_API_KEY` está presente, sin necesitar `base_url` override en config. Esto contradice el "Pitfall #2" del plan TI-1421 original — no era pitfall real. Si solo se setea `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, OpenFang usa OpenRouter con su default model (`gemini-2.5-flash`), no el modelo del config.toml (que se ignora si el path es incorrecto — ver punto 3).
16	
17	5. **Default bind interno es `127.0.0.1:50051` (HTTP API) y `127.0.0.1:4200` (OFP P2P)** — solo loopback dentro del container. Para health checks externos hay que setear `api_listen = "0.0.0.0:50051"` y `[network] listen_addr = "0.0.0.0:4200"` en el config (que se carga si el path es correcto, ver punto 3). El `/data/daemon.json` (creado en runtime) muestra el bind real.
18	
19	6. **Slack Socket Mode no requiere ingress HTTP** — outbound WebSocket. Por eso la VM funciona sin LB y sin abrir puertos.
20	
21	7. **9 bundled hands** vienen con la imagen (lead, collector, predictor, researcher, twitter, browser, trader, infisical-sync) + 25 extension templates. Walking skeleton tiene OpenFang funcional sin instalar nada extra.

Hallazgos confirmados al levantar OpenFang v0.5.9 en VM Rocky Linux 9 (apps/ai/):

1. **Imagen `ghcr.io/RightNow-AI/openfang:0.5.9` NO es pública** — retorna `unauthorized` al `docker pull`. El propio `docker-compose.yml` del repo lo dice ("GHCR image is not yet public, build from source"). Workaround: clonar repo + `docker build`. Issue tracker: https://github.com/RightNow-AI/openfang/issues/12

2. **Build Rust release en e2-medium (2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM) toma ~80 minutos** con `--build-arg LTO=false --build-arg CODEGEN_UNITS=16`. Imagen final pesa 1.74 GB (Rust + python3 + nodejs + wasmtime con todos los features). Sin esos build args (LTO=true, CODEGEN_UNITS=1) probablemente OOM. Para CI/CD futuro: usar machine más grande o pre-built image en AR Liftit.

3. **OpenFang busca config en `~/.openfang/config.toml`** (= `/root/.openfang/config.toml` cuando container corre como root). `OPENFANG_HOME=/data` (env del Dockerfile) es para el **data store** (sqlite, workspaces, daemon.json) — NO para config. Si montas config en `/data/.openfang/config.toml` se ignora silenciosamente.

4. **OpenFang autodetecta el provider LLM por env vars** — escoge basado en cuál de `{OPENROUTER,ANTHROPIC,OPENAI,GROQ}_API_KEY` está presente, sin necesitar `base_url` override en config. Esto contradice el "Pitfall #2" del plan TI-1421 original — no era pitfall real. Si solo se setea `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, OpenFang usa OpenRouter con su default model (`gemini-2.5-flash`), no el modelo del config.toml (que se ignora si el path es incorrecto — ver punto 3).

5. **Default bind interno es `127.0.0.1:50051` (HTTP API) y `127.0.0.1:4200` (OFP P2P)** — solo loopback dentro del container. Para health checks externos hay que setear `api_listen = "0.0.0.0:50051"` y `[network] listen_addr = "0.0.0.0:4200"` en el config (que se carga si el path es correcto, ver punto 3). El `/data/daemon.json` (creado en runtime) muestra el bind real.

6. **Slack Socket Mode no requiere ingress HTTP** — outbound WebSocket. Por eso la VM funciona sin LB y sin abrir puertos.

7. **9 bundled hands** vienen con la imagen (lead, collector, predictor, researcher, twitter, browser, trader, infisical-sync) + 25 extension templates. Walking skeleton tiene OpenFang funcional sin instalar nada extra.

# OpenFang Hand — walking skeleton config
# Bind on 0.0.0.0 so the container exposes ports outside the container netns

api_key_env = "OPENROUTER_API_KEY"
base_url    = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"

[memory]

[network]

Hallazgos confirmados al levantar OpenFang v0.5.9 en VM Rocky Linux 9 (apps/ai/):

1. **Imagen `ghcr.io/RightNow-AI/openfang:0.5.9` NO es pública** — retorna `unauthorized` al `docker pull`. El propio `docker-compose.yml` del repo lo dice ("GHCR image is not yet public, build from source"). Workaround: clonar repo + `docker build`. Issue tracker: https://github.com/RightNow-AI/openfang/issues/12

2. **Build Rust release en e2-medium (2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM) toma ~80 minutos** con `--build-arg LTO=false --build-arg CODEGEN_UNITS=16`. Imagen final pesa 1.74 GB (Rust + python3 + nodejs + wasmtime con todos los features). Sin esos build args (LTO=true, CODEGEN_UNITS=1) probablemente OOM. Para CI/CD futuro: usar machine más grande o pre-built image en AR Liftit.

3. **OpenFang busca config en `~/.openfang/config.toml`** (= `/root/.openfang/config.toml` cuando container corre como root). `OPENFANG_HOME=/data` (env del Dockerfile) es para el **data store** (sqlite, workspaces, daemon.json) — NO para config. Si montas config en `/data/.openfang/config.toml` se ignora silenciosamente.

4. **OpenFang autodetecta el provider LLM por env vars** — escoge basado en cuál de `{OPENROUTER,ANTHROPIC,OPENAI,GROQ}_API_KEY` está presente, sin necesitar `base_url` override en config. Esto contradice el "Pitfall #2" del plan TI-1421 original — no era pitfall real. Si solo se setea `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, OpenFang usa OpenRouter con su default model (`gemini-2.5-flash`), no el modelo del config.toml (que se ignora si el path es incorrecto — ver punto 3).

5. **Default bind interno es `127.0.0.1:50051` (HTTP API) y `127.0.0.1:4200` (OFP P2P)** — solo loopback dentro del container. Para health checks externos hay que setear `api_listen = "0.0.0.0:50051"` y `[network] listen_addr = "0.0.0.0:4200"` en el config (que se carga si el path es correcto, ver punto 3). El `/data/daemon.json` (creado en runtime) muestra el bind real.

6. **Slack Socket Mode no requiere ingress HTTP** — outbound WebSocket. Por eso la VM funciona sin LB y sin abrir puertos.

7. **9 bundled hands** vienen con la imagen (lead, collector, predictor, researcher, twitter, browser, trader, infisical-sync) + 25 extension templates. Walking skeleton tiene OpenFang funcional sin instalar nada extra.

message.content: Install to workspace, cómo hago eso?

content.text:
En la sidebar izquierda del app config (api.slack.com/apps/TU_APP):

1. **Settings → Install App** → botón "Install to Workspace"
2. O equivalente: **Features → OAuth & Permissions** → arriba botón "Install to Workspace"

Slack te mostrará un screen de permisos (los scopes que configuraste) → "Allow" → te lleva de vuelta y ahora verás el **Bot User OAuth Token** (`xoxb-...`) en OAuth & Permissions.

Si el botón está disabled, falta algo:
- No agregaste Bot Token Scopes todavía
- El workspace requiere approval de admin (te aparecerá "Request to Install")

message.content: Invita el bot a #monitoreo_infraestructura cómo hago eso?

content.text:
Desde Slack client, en el canal `#monitoreo_infraestructura`:

**Opción 1 (más rápida):** escribe en el canal
```
/invite @nombre_de_tu_bot
```

El nombre del bot es el que pusiste en la app config (Basic Information → App Name, o Display Information).

**Opción 2:** click al nombre del canal arriba → tab **Integrations** → **Add apps** → busca tu app → Add.

Si no aparece en la lista de apps, verifica que ya ejecutaste "Install to Workspace".

services:
  openfang:
    image: openfang-local:0.5.9
    container_name: openfang
    env_file: .env
    volumes:
      - ./config.toml:/data/config.toml:ro
      - ./openfang-data:/data
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:4200:4200"      # OFP — loopback only
      - "127.0.0.1:50051:50051"    # HTTP API — loopback only
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - phoenix

  phoenix:
    image: arizephoenix/phoenix:14.8.0
    container_name: phoenix
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:6006:6006"      # UI — loopback only (D-33)
      - "127.0.0.1:4317:4317"      # OTLP gRPC — loopback only
    volumes:
      - ./phoenix-data:/mnt/data
    restart: unless-stopped

**Slack conectado ✓** — `Slack Socket Mode connected`, bot `U07HS8YS23A` autenticado, bridge activo.

Para ver la UI web: la dashboard escucha en `127.0.0.1:50051` dentro de la VM (no expuesta públicamente). Abre un **SSH port-forward** desde tu laptop:

```bash
ssh -L 50051:127.0.0.1:50051 openfang
```

Dejando ese terminal abierto, abre en tu browser local: **http://localhost:50051**

La UI probablemente pida login (hay strings de `dashboard login` + `openfang_session` cookie). Si pide credenciales y no las tienes, dime y te ayudo a setearlas con `openfang config set-key` o el flujo de `openfang auth`.

También puedes probar el E2E de Slack ya mismo: mencionalo en `#monitoreo_infraestructura` con `@<nombre del bot> hola` — debería responder usando qwen vía OpenRouter.

- **"Free endpoints that may train on request data"** (obligatorio)
- **"Free endpoints that may publish prompts"** (algunos providers)

**Consideración de seguridad:** este bot va a procesar eventualmente logs/alertas/métricas de infra de Liftit. Activar esos toggles significa que OpenAI/Anthropic/etc. pueden **retener y entrenar** con los prompts, y algunos **publicar** a datasets públicos. Para un ops agent con contexto interno, eso es un leak potencial.

**Recomiendo fuerte `google/gemini-2.5-flash` paid** — $0.075/1M input, ~$1-2/mes para uso típico de walking skeleton, sin consent de training. Trade-off: pagás dólares por mes vs. exponer data operacional de Liftit.

¿Cambio a gemini-2.5-flash o preferís activar los toggles free para pruebas iniciales con mensajes dummy y migrar a paid después?

content.text:
Buen pivote. Ese es exactamente el scope de **TI-1425** (Parte 2). Esto convierte el bloqueo de OpenRouter en una feature: LLM local, sin data leaks, costo fijo.

**Arquitectura propuesta (walking skeleton, sin MIG aún):**
- VM GCP dedicada con GPU → corre **vLLM** (OpenAI-compatible) → OpenFang apunta a `http://<vm-ip>:8000/v1`
- `ai-infra-orchestrator` (CPU actual) queda sin cambios, solo se le cambia `base_url` + `model`

**3 decisiones que necesito:**

1. **GPU:** `L4 24GB` (~$0.65/hr, cómodo para 7B) vs `T4 16GB` (~$0.35/hr, apretado para 7B FP16) — recomiendo L4
2. **Modelo:** `Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` (como plan original), `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`, o `Qwen2.5-Coder-7B` (mejor para ops/infra) — recomiendo Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
3. **Scope hoy:** VM siempre-on vs. auto-stop nocturno vs. MIG scale-to-zero — recomiendo siempre-on para walking skeleton, MIG después

Antes de Terraform, valido **GPU quota** en `prod-apps-454414` us-east1. ¿Confirmas L4 + Qwen2.5-7B + siempre-on?

# apps/ai — AI Infrastructure VMs

## What This Module Does
Provisions VMs that host AI / LLM ops tooling for Liftit (OpenFang Hand orchestrator + Arize Phoenix observability stack). Walking-skeleton scope: VM only, no load balancer, no DNS — Slack Socket Mode + outbound LLM calls do not require ingress.

## State
- **Backend**: GCS bucket `liftit-tf-state`, prefix `apps/ai`
- **Workspaces**: prod (only)

## VMs
| App | Env | Machine | Zone | Disk |
|-----|-----|---------|------|------|
| ai-infra-orchestrator | prod | e2-medium | us-east1-b | pd-ssd 50 GB |

## Resources Created
- VM via `tf-modules//vm` (Rocky Linux 9, CMEK encrypted boot disk, daily backup, deletion protection, alerting)
- Static internal IP, network tag `ssh` (no LB ingress)

## Bootstrap
The module does NOT install Docker / OpenFang / Phoenix. Provisioning of the container stack is performed manually over SSH after `terraform apply` (Option B per TI-1421 Parte 1 walking skeleton).

## Dependencies (remote state)
- `org/projects` (folders) — workspace `gen`
- `networking/vpc` — workspace `prod`
- `sec/kms` — workspace `sec`
- `iam/service-accounts` — workspace `prod`
- `sec/backup` — workspace `prod`

## Providers
- Terraform `~> 1.14`, Google `~> 7.0`

content.text:
**Preemptible L4 en us-east1 = 32 ✓.** 

Falta **G2 CPUs** en us-east1 (filtro: `G2 CPUs`). Es la quota del machine family que lleva el L4 — sin ésta, el template no arranca. Verifícala mientras avanzo.

Ya leí `vm.tf` — el módulo `tf-modules//vm` actual **no cubre GPU ni MIG**, así que el vLLM va en un archivo nuevo `apps/ai/vllm.tf` con recursos nativos GCP (`google_compute_instance_template` + `google_compute_instance_group_manager` + health check).

**Diseño del módulo vLLM (walking skeleton):**

| Componente | Decisión |
|---|---|
| Imagen | `deeplearning-platform-release/common-cu124-debian-11-py310` (NVIDIA driver + CUDA + Docker pre-instalados) |
| Machine | `g2-standard-4` (4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM, 1 × L4) |
| Scheduling | `SPOT` + `on_host_maintenance = TERMINATE` + `automatic_restart = false` |
| Disco | 100 GB pd-ssd (modelo 14 GB + vLLM image + OS) |
| MIG | size=1, auto-repair con health check `:8000/health` |
| Static IP | interna fija → OpenFang apunta estable aunque se recree VM |
| Bootstrap | startup script: `docker run --gpus all -p 8000:8000 -v /models:/models vllm/vllm-openai --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` |
| Firewall | rule `vllm-api` permitiendo `:8000` desde subnet de `apps-prod` (orchestrator) |

¿Te cuadra el diseño o ajustamos algo antes de que escriba el Terraform?

# sec/firewall — VPC Firewall Rules & Appliance

## What This Module Does
Manages VPC firewall rules per workspace, deploys a firewall VM appliance in the security project, and configures VPN/Wireguard routes.

## State
- **Backend**: GCS bucket `liftit-tf-state`, prefix `sec/firewall`
- **Workspaces**: qa, staging, prod, sha, sec

## Resources Created
- Firewall rules per workspace: SSH, web-public, web-private, HTTP-backend, PostgreSQL, RDP, Redis, MongoDB, AMQP, GKE nodes (TCP/UDP), Wrenai-poc, NFS
- Firewall VM appliance (sec workspace only): e2-small, IP forwarding enabled
- VPN route: 10.220.1.0/24 via firewall VM
- Wireguard route: 10.220.2.0/24 via firewall VM
- Cloudflare A record for `acceso` subdomain (sec only)

## Dependencies (remote state)
| Name | Prefix | Workspace | Provides |
|------|--------|-----------|----------|
| folders | `project` | gen | gcp_folder_id, gcp_projects_ids |
| vpc | `networking/vpc` | current | vpc_id, network_cidr, subnet_ids |
| vpc-sec | `networking/vpc` | sec | network CIDR |
| kms | `sec/kms` | sec | KMS keys |
| sa | `iam-service-accounts` | current | SA emails |
| dns | `networking/dns` | gen | zone IDs, API token |
| backup | `sec/backup` | current | snapshot schedules |

## Key Files
- `fw-vpc.tf` — Firewall rules module (for_each)
- `vm.tf` — Firewall VM appliance + routes
- `cloudflare.tf` — DNS record for VPN access

## Providers
- Terraform `~> 1.14`, Google `~> 7.0`, Cloudflare `~> 4.0`

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
exec > >(tee -a /var/log/vllm-startup.log) 2>&1

echo "[vllm-startup] Starting at $(date -Is)"

until nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; do
  echo "[vllm-startup] waiting for NVIDIA driver..."
  sleep 5
done
nvidia-smi

systemctl enable --now docker

if docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -q '^vllm$'; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] vllm container already running — nothing to do"
  exit 0
fi

docker rm -f vllm >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

mkdir -p /var/lib/vllm/cache
chmod 755 /var/lib/vllm/cache

VLLM_IMAGE="vllm/vllm-openai:v0.6.3"
docker pull "${VLLM_IMAGE}"

docker run -d \
  --name vllm \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --gpus all \
  --ipc=host \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /var/lib/vllm/cache:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  "${VLLM_IMAGE}" \
  --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
  --served-model-name qwen-2.5-7b \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --trust-remote-code

echo "[vllm-startup] container started; first boot downloads ~14 GB model"

content.text:
Sí es posible, pero con trade-off que quiero transparentar:

| Opción | Cold boot | Estándar repo |
|---|---|---|
| **Rocky 9 + install en startup** | ~15-20 min (driver NVIDIA + Docker + nvidia-container-toolkit + vLLM + 14 GB modelo) | ✓ |
| **DLVM Debian** (actual) | ~5 min (drivers pre-instalados) | ✗ |
| **Rocky 9 + golden image con Packer** | ~5 min | ✓ pero requiere pipeline Packer extra |

Con spot + MIG, si preemption ocurre, Rocky 9 standard tarda 15-20 min en volver a responder. Durante ese tiempo el bot no funciona.

**Opciones pragmáticas:**
1. Rocky 9 standard ahora, Packer golden image después (TI separado)
2. DLVM ahora para iterar rápido, migrar a Rocky 9 + Packer al final de TI-1425

¿Cuál prefieres?

For running Large Language Models (LLMs) on Rocky Linux within Google Cloud Platform (GCP), the most direct solution is the RLC Pro AI image provided by CIQ, the official support partner for Rocky Linux. 
CIQ
CIQ
 +1
Optimized Rocky Linux LLM Images
Standard Rocky Linux images require manual setup of drivers and libraries. However, specialized versions simplify LLM deployment:
RLC Pro AI (Recommended): This enterprise-grade image is built specifically for AI/ML workloads. It includes a pre-validated NVIDIA stack and a customized Linux kernel to maximize GPU performance and reduce configuration time.
Rocky Linux (NVIDIA) Family: Google provides specialized image families such as rocky-linux-9-optimized-gcp-nvidia which come with pre-installed NVIDIA drivers for Compute Engine.
HPC-Optimized Images: For clustered LLM training or high-throughput inference, Google offers a Rocky Linux 8 HPC VM image optimized for high-bandwidth networking and MPI benchmarks. 
Google Cloud
Google Cloud
 +4
How to Deploy
GCP Marketplace: Search for "Rocky Linux" or "CIQ" in the Google Cloud Marketplace to find pre-configured AI images.
CLI Deployment: You can create an instance using the Google Cloud CLI by specifying the rocky-linux-cloud project.
LLM Frameworks: Once the VM is running, you can install serving frameworks like Ollama or vLLM to run models like Llama or Gemma. 
CIQ
CIQ
 +4
Security Note: Ensure your Rocky Linux images are updated to at least version v20250912 to address critical kernel vulnerabilities.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
exec > >(tee -a /var/log/vllm-startup.log) 2>&1

echo "[vllm-startup] Starting at $(date -Is)"

until nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; do
  echo "[vllm-startup] waiting for NVIDIA driver..."
  sleep 5
done
nvidia-smi

systemctl enable --now docker

if docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -q '^vllm$'; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] vllm container already running — nothing to do"
  exit 0
fi

docker rm -f vllm >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

mkdir -p /var/lib/vllm/cache
chmod 755 /var/lib/vllm/cache

VLLM_IMAGE="vllm/vllm-openai:v0.6.3"
docker pull "${VLLM_IMAGE}"

docker run -d \
  --name vllm \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --gpus all \
  --ipc=host \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /var/lib/vllm/cache:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  "${VLLM_IMAGE}" \
  --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
  --served-model-name qwen-2.5-7b \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --trust-remote-code

echo "[vllm-startup] container started; first boot downloads ~14 GB model"

  systemctl restart docker
fi

if docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -q '^vllm$'; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] vllm container already running — nothing to do"
  exit 0

echo "[vllm-startup] container started; first boot downloads ~14 GB model (~5-10 min)"

**Encontré el problema real: `ZONE_RESOURCE_POOL_EXHAUSTED`** — `us-east1-b` no tiene capacidad de L4 spot en este momento.

```
"A g2-standard-4 VM instance with 1 nvidia-l4 accelerator(s) is currently unavailable in us-east1-b"
```

**Fix recomendado: MIG regional multi-zona.** Cambiar de MIG zonal a **regional** que intenta en `us-east1-b`, `-c`, `-d` — max probabilidad de encontrar capacity spot. También aprovecho para quitar `enable-oslogin = TRUE` (que bloquea SSH con user `jhon`).

Un solo apply que recrea el MIG. ¿Procedo?

content.text:
Opciones realistas con Qwen2.5-7B (requiere ≥16GB VRAM FP16, ~6GB si quantizado):

| GPU | VRAM | Spot | Capacidad us-east1 | Caveat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **T4** (`n1-standard-4` + 1 T4) | 16GB | ~$0.19/hr | **Alta** (abundante) | Apretado para 7B FP16 → usar variante **AWQ** quantized (~6GB) |
| L4 (actual) | 24GB | ~$0.26/hr | **Baja ahora** | Stockout |
| A100 40GB (`a2-highgpu-1g`) | 40GB | ~$1.2/hr | Media | 5x más caro, overkill |
| A100 80GB (`a2-ultragpu-1g`) | 80GB | ~$2/hr | Baja | Caro |

**Recomendación: T4 + Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ** (variante quantized oficial de Qwen, ~6GB). Ventajas:
- Capacidad GPU abundante (T4 es lo más desplegado)
- Costo más bajo (~$0.19/hr)
- Performance similar para tareas ops (AWQ ≈1-2% accuracy drop)

Machine type: `n1-standard-4` (4 vCPU, 15 GB) + 1 × T4. Cambio también el modelo a `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ`.

message.content: Pero la versión awq tiene el mismo performance y efectividad?

content.text:
Honesto: **no es exactamente igual, pero la diferencia es marginal para nuestro caso**.

**Datos de benchmarks (Qwen2.5-7B AWQ vs FP16):**
- MMLU: ~1-2% peor
- HumanEval: ~1-3% peor
- Tareas conversacionales y razonamiento simple: prácticamente indistinguible

**Trade-off concreto:**
- **AWQ puede flaquear en**: razonamiento matemático multi-paso complejo, cadenas de lógica larga, tareas donde cada token importa.
- **AWQ es transparente para**: leer logs, identificar patrones, llamar MCP servers, responder queries ops típicas.

Para un bot que consulta métricas, resume alertas y llama tools (caso ops tuyo), es indistinguible en práctica.

**Si quieres cero compromisos**, las alternativas son:
- **L4 on-demand** ($0.7/hr) — FP16 full, disponible ahora, 3.5x más caro que T4 spot
- **A100 40GB spot** ($1.2/hr) — FP16 full, sobrada VRAM, ~6x más caro que T4 spot — *si hay capacidad spot*

¿Quieres ir con T4+AWQ (pragmático), L4 on-demand (full, caro), o esperar spot L4?

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
exec > >(tee -a /var/log/vllm-startup.log) 2>&1

echo "[vllm-startup] starting at $(date -Is)"

until nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; do
  echo "[vllm-startup] waiting for NVIDIA driver..."
  sleep 5
done
nvidia-smi

if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] installing Docker CE"
  dnf install -y dnf-plugins-core
  dnf config-manager --add-repo https://download.docker.com/linux/centos/docker-ce.repo
  dnf install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io
fi
systemctl enable --now docker

if ! command -v nvidia-ctk >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] installing nvidia-container-toolkit"
  curl -sL https://nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/stable/rpm/nvidia-container-toolkit.repo \
    > /etc/yum.repos.d/nvidia-container-toolkit.repo
  dnf install -y nvidia-container-toolkit
  nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker
  systemctl restart docker
fi

if docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -q '^vllm$'; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] vllm container already running — nothing to do"
  exit 0
fi

docker rm -f vllm >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

mkdir -p /var/lib/vllm/cache
chmod 755 /var/lib/vllm/cache

VLLM_IMAGE="vllm/vllm-openai:v0.6.3"
docker pull "${VLLM_IMAGE}"

docker run -d \
  --name vllm \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --gpus all \
  --ipc=host \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /var/lib/vllm/cache:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  "${VLLM_IMAGE}" \
  --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
  --served-model-name qwen-2.5-7b \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --trust-remote-code

echo "[vllm-startup] container started; first boot downloads ~14 GB model (~5-10 min)"

content.text:
**Constraint de GCP: T4 solo se puede attach a máquinas N1.** Es arquitectura del proveedor.

Mapping GPU ↔ Machine family:
- **T4, P4, P100, V100, K80** → solo N1 (attach style)
- **L4** → solo G2 (integrada) — stockout spot ahora
- **A100** → solo A2 (integrada) — $1.2+/hr spot
- **H100** → solo A3 (integrada) — muy caro + cuota difícil

Para GPU moderna tendrías que ir a L4/A100/H100, pero eso nos devuelve al problema original (caro o stockout). Para inference vLLM el CPU del host casi no importa (todo corre en GPU), así que N1 Skylake no degrada performance.

VM ya RUNNING en `10.212.0.35`. Monitoreo startup del script.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
exec > >(tee -a /var/log/vllm-startup.log) 2>&1

echo "[vllm-startup] starting at $(date -Is)"

until nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; do
  echo "[vllm-startup] waiting for NVIDIA driver..."
  sleep 5
done
nvidia-smi

if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] installing Docker CE"
  dnf install -y dnf-plugins-core
  dnf config-manager --add-repo https://download.docker.com/linux/centos/docker-ce.repo
  dnf install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io
fi
systemctl enable --now docker

if ! command -v nvidia-ctk >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] installing nvidia-container-toolkit"
  curl -sL https://nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/stable/rpm/nvidia-container-toolkit.repo \
    > /etc/yum.repos.d/nvidia-container-toolkit.repo
  dnf install -y nvidia-container-toolkit
  nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker
  systemctl restart docker
fi

if docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -q '^vllm$'; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] vllm container already running — nothing to do"
  exit 0
fi

docker rm -f vllm >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

mkdir -p /var/lib/vllm/cache
chmod 755 /var/lib/vllm/cache

VLLM_IMAGE="vllm/vllm-openai:v0.6.3"
docker pull "${VLLM_IMAGE}"

docker run -d \
  --name vllm \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --gpus all \
  --ipc=host \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /var/lib/vllm/cache:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  "${VLLM_IMAGE}" \
  --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ \
  --quantization awq \
  --dtype half \
  --served-model-name qwen-2.5-7b \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --trust-remote-code

echo "[vllm-startup] container started; first boot downloads ~6 GB AWQ model (~2-4 min)"

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
exec > >(tee -a /var/log/vllm-startup.log) 2>&1

echo "[vllm-startup] starting at $(date -Is)"

until nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; do
  echo "[vllm-startup] waiting for NVIDIA driver..."
  sleep 5
done
nvidia-smi

if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] installing Docker CE"
  dnf install -y dnf-plugins-core
  dnf config-manager --add-repo https://download.docker.com/linux/centos/docker-ce.repo
  dnf install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io
fi
systemctl enable --now docker

if ! command -v nvidia-ctk >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] installing nvidia-container-toolkit"
  curl -sL https://nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/stable/rpm/nvidia-container-toolkit.repo \
    > /etc/yum.repos.d/nvidia-container-toolkit.repo
  dnf install -y nvidia-container-toolkit
  nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker
  systemctl restart docker
fi

if docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -q '^vllm$'; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] vllm container already running — nothing to do"
  exit 0
fi

docker rm -f vllm >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

mkdir -p /var/lib/vllm/cache
chmod 755 /var/lib/vllm/cache

VLLM_IMAGE="vllm/vllm-openai:v0.6.3"
docker pull "${VLLM_IMAGE}"

docker run -d \
  --name vllm \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --gpus all \
  --ipc=host \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /var/lib/vllm/cache:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  "${VLLM_IMAGE}" \
  --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ \
  --quantization awq \
  --dtype half \
  --served-model-name qwen-2.5-7b \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser hermes

echo "[vllm-startup] container started; first boot downloads ~6 GB AWQ model (~2-4 min)"

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
exec > >(tee -a /var/log/vllm-startup.log) 2>&1

echo "[vllm-startup] starting at $(date -Is)"

until nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; do
  echo "[vllm-startup] waiting for NVIDIA driver..."
  sleep 5
done
nvidia-smi

if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] installing Docker CE"
  dnf install -y dnf-plugins-core
  dnf config-manager --add-repo https://download.docker.com/linux/centos/docker-ce.repo
  dnf install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io
fi
systemctl enable --now docker

if ! command -v nvidia-ctk >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] installing nvidia-container-toolkit"
  curl -sL https://nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/stable/rpm/nvidia-container-toolkit.repo \
    > /etc/yum.repos.d/nvidia-container-toolkit.repo
  dnf install -y nvidia-container-toolkit
  nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker
  systemctl restart docker
fi

if docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -q '^vllm$'; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] vllm container already running — nothing to do"
  exit 0
fi

docker rm -f vllm >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

mkdir -p /var/lib/vllm/cache
chmod 755 /var/lib/vllm/cache

VLLM_IMAGE="vllm/vllm-openai:v0.6.3"
docker pull "${VLLM_IMAGE}"

docker run -d \
  --name vllm \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --gpus all \
  --ipc=host \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /var/lib/vllm/cache:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  "${VLLM_IMAGE}" \
  --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ \
  --quantization awq \
  --dtype half \
  --served-model-name qwen-2.5-7b \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser hermes

echo "[vllm-startup] container started; first boot downloads ~6 GB AWQ model (~2-4 min)"

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
exec > >(tee -a /var/log/vllm-startup.log) 2>&1

echo "[vllm-startup] starting at $(date -Is)"

until nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; do
  echo "[vllm-startup] waiting for NVIDIA driver..."
  sleep 5
done
nvidia-smi

if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] installing Docker CE"
  dnf install -y dnf-plugins-core
  dnf config-manager --add-repo https://download.docker.com/linux/centos/docker-ce.repo
  dnf install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io
fi
systemctl enable --now docker

if ! command -v nvidia-ctk >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] installing nvidia-container-toolkit"
  curl -sL https://nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/stable/rpm/nvidia-container-toolkit.repo \
    > /etc/yum.repos.d/nvidia-container-toolkit.repo
  dnf install -y nvidia-container-toolkit
  nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker
  systemctl restart docker
fi

if docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -q '^vllm$'; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] vllm container already running — nothing to do"
  exit 0
fi

docker rm -f vllm >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

mkdir -p /var/lib/vllm/cache
chmod 755 /var/lib/vllm/cache

VLLM_IMAGE="vllm/vllm-openai:latest"
docker pull "${VLLM_IMAGE}"

docker run -d \
  --name vllm \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --gpus all \
  --ipc=host \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /var/lib/vllm/cache:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  "${VLLM_IMAGE}" \
  --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ \
  --quantization awq \
  --dtype half \
  --served-model-name qwen-2.5-7b \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser hermes

echo "[vllm-startup] container started; first boot downloads ~6 GB AWQ model (~2-4 min)"

attachment.prompt: Por qué se volvió a crear otra máquina?

content.text:
**Diagnóstico:** el MIG está en **loop de auto-repair** porque las VMs tardan más en pasar health que `initial_delay_sec=900` (15 min). Cuando el initial_delay se agota y `:8000/health` aún no responde, MIG considera que la VM está broken y la recrea.

El cold boot incluye: install Docker + nvidia-container-toolkit (~2 min) + **pull vllm:v0.8.5 (~8 min por ser imagen grande)** + download Qwen2.5-7B-AWQ (~1 min) + vLLM warmup (~2 min) = **~13 min**, cerca del límite.

**Fix inmediato:** subir `initial_delay_sec` a 1800 (30 min). Aplico.

input.content:
# packer/vllm — Golden image for vLLM inference

## What this builds
GCP custom image based on `rocky-linux-9-optimized-gcp-nvidia-580` with:
- Docker CE + containerd
- nvidia-container-toolkit configured as Docker runtime
- `vllm/vllm-openai:<version>` pre-pulled into local Docker cache

Result: image family `vllm-prod` in project `prod-apps-454414`, usable by `apps/ai/vllm.tf` instead of the public Rocky NVIDIA image.

## Why
Startup script in `apps/ai/files/vllm-startup.sh` takes ~13 min cold-boot because it installs Docker, nvidia-container-toolkit, and pulls the ~10 GB vLLM image every time. Pre-baking these into a golden image reduces cold boot to ~1-2 min.

## Build
```
cd packer/vllm
packer init .
packer build -var "vllm_version=v0.8.5" vllm.pkr.hcl
```

Build takes ~10-12 min (same as a cold boot, but only once per image rev).

## Consume from terraform
Update `apps/ai/vllm.tf`:
```hcl
data "google_compute_image" "vllm_base" {
  project = "prod-apps-454414"
  family  = "vllm-prod"
}
```

And simplify `apps/ai/files/vllm-startup.sh` to only do `docker run` (skip the dnf installs).

## Rebuild triggers
Rebuild the image when:
- vLLM version changes
- NVIDIA driver or Rocky base image gets a security update
- nvidia-container-toolkit has a breaking change

## Not pre-cached
The model weights (`Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ`) are NOT baked into the image. They download from HuggingFace on first boot (~1 min) and persist in `/var/lib/vllm/cache` across restarts. This keeps the image slim and makes model swaps cheap.

**Bosquejo Packer creado** (no aplicado, solo archivos):

```
packer/vllm/
├── vllm.pkr.hcl       # main template
├── files/prebuild.sh  # script executed on build VM
└── README.md          # how-to + consumption notes
```

- Base: `rocky-linux-9-optimized-gcp-nvidia-580` (misma que ahora)
- Preinstala: Docker + nvidia-container-toolkit + `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.8.5` pre-pulled

- Build time: ~10 min one-time
- Cold boot post-golden: ~1-2 min (vs 13 min actual)

**Para usarlo después:**
1. `cd packer/vllm && packer init . && packer build -var "vllm_version=v0.8.5" vllm.pkr.hcl`
2. Update `apps/ai/vllm.tf` → data source apunta a `project=prod-apps-454414, family=vllm-prod`

Config mount es read-only. Y no veo `max_tokens` como campo del `default_model` en OpenFang (no está expuesto en config). Callejón sin salida fácil.

**Mi recomendación firme ahora:** vamos a Packer. Ya probamos 5 iteraciones en vllm.tf y quedan más:
- Tendría que subir `max-model-len` a 16384 (requiere recrear VM = 10+ min pull)
- Si crashea de nuevo por el bug shape que vimos, tercera iteración
- Sin Packer, cada iteración cuesta 10-15 min de pull

**Propuesta:**
1. `target_size=0` → detiene VM + costo (~10 seg)
2. `packer build` → ~10 min one-time
3. Update `vllm.tf` apuntando a golden image + simplifico startup (cold boot ~2 min)
4. Uso `--max-model-len 16384` desde el inicio
5. Si todo bien, E2E. Si falla, segundo intento es 2 min, no 13.

¿Lo hacemos?

content.text:
Correcto, con `v0.6.3` tuve el bug `shape (646,) into (512,)` (no OOM — bug XFormers). Con `latest` el `EngineCore crashed` sin stack claro (puede ser OOM, pero no confirmado).

**Análisis honesto sobre 16k en T4+AWQ:**
- VRAM T4 = 15 GB; modelo AWQ = 5.2 GB; quedan ~9 GB para KV cache
- Qwen2.5-7B con GQA = ~64 KB/token → 16k tokens = ~1 GB (cabe holgado)
- El problema previo con v0.6.3 NO era OOM — era bug de biblioteca
- v0.8.5 probablemente lo resuelve, pero **no lo puedo garantizar**

**Alternativa sin recrear VM:** reducir el context de OpenFang deshabilitando hands. Los 60 tools vienen de 9 bundled hands (browser, trader, twitter, predictor, etc.) que no necesitamos para ops. Deshabilitando 5-6 de ellos, el system prompt baja de 10k a ~4-5k tokens → cabe en 12288 con margen.

```
openfang hand deactivate browser
openfang hand deactivate trader
openfang hand deactivate twitter
openfang hand deactivate predictor
# etc.
```

**Opciones:**
1. **Deshabilitar hands** (2 min, sin tocar infra) — pragmático
2. **Packer con 16k** (~15 min, más robusto) — correcto a largo plazo

¿Probamos (1) primero? Si va, seguimos con Packer para el cold boot.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
exec > >(tee -a /var/log/vllm-prebuild.log) 2>&1

echo "[prebuild] starting at $(date -Is)"

nvidia-smi

dnf install -y dnf-plugins-core
dnf config-manager --add-repo https://download.docker.com/linux/centos/docker-ce.repo
dnf install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io
systemctl enable --now docker

curl -sL https://nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/stable/rpm/nvidia-container-toolkit.repo \
  > /etc/yum.repos.d/nvidia-container-toolkit.repo
dnf install -y nvidia-container-toolkit
nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker
systemctl restart docker

VLLM_IMAGE="vllm/vllm-openai:${VLLM_VERSION:-v0.8.5}"
echo "[prebuild] pulling ${VLLM_IMAGE}"
docker pull "${VLLM_IMAGE}"
docker images

dnf clean all

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
exec > >(tee -a /var/log/vllm-prebuild.log) 2>&1

echo "[prebuild] starting at $(date -Is)"

nvidia-smi

dnf install -y dnf-plugins-core
dnf config-manager --add-repo https://download.docker.com/linux/centos/docker-ce.repo
dnf install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io
systemctl enable --now docker

curl -sL https://nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/stable/rpm/nvidia-container-toolkit.repo \
  > /etc/yum.repos.d/nvidia-container-toolkit.repo
dnf install -y nvidia-container-toolkit
nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker
systemctl restart docker

VLLM_IMAGE="vllm/vllm-openai:${VLLM_VERSION:-v0.8.5}"
echo "[prebuild] pulling ${VLLM_IMAGE}"
docker pull "${VLLM_IMAGE}"
docker images

dnf clean all
rm -rf /var/cache/dnf

echo "[prebuild] done; image ready for snapshot"

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
exec > >(tee -a /var/log/vllm-startup.log) 2>&1

echo "[vllm-startup] starting at $(date -Is)"

until nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; do
  echo "[vllm-startup] waiting for NVIDIA driver..."
  sleep 5
done
nvidia-smi

if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] installing Docker CE"
  dnf install -y dnf-plugins-core
  dnf config-manager --add-repo https://download.docker.com/linux/centos/docker-ce.repo
  dnf install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io
fi
systemctl enable --now docker

if ! command -v nvidia-ctk >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] installing nvidia-container-toolkit"
  curl -sL https://nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/stable/rpm/nvidia-container-toolkit.repo \
    > /etc/yum.repos.d/nvidia-container-toolkit.repo
  dnf install -y nvidia-container-toolkit
  nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker
  systemctl restart docker
fi

if docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -q '^vllm$'; then
  echo "[vllm-startup] vllm container already running — nothing to do"
  exit 0
fi

docker rm -f vllm >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

mkdir -p /var/lib/vllm/cache
chmod 755 /var/lib/vllm/cache

VLLM_IMAGE="vllm/vllm-openai:v0.8.5"
docker pull "${VLLM_IMAGE}"

docker run -d \
  --name vllm \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --gpus all \
  --ipc=host \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /var/lib/vllm/cache:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  "${VLLM_IMAGE}" \
  --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ \
  --quantization awq \
  --dtype half \
  --served-model-name qwen-2.5-7b \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 \
  --max-model-len 12288 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser hermes

echo "[vllm-startup] container started; first boot downloads ~6 GB AWQ model (~2-4 min)"

feat(packer/vllm): golden image builder for vLLM inference VMs

Adds a Packer template that bakes Docker CE, nvidia-container-toolkit,
and the `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.8.5` image on top of Rocky Linux 9 NVIDIA
(`rocky-linux-9-optimized-gcp-nvidia-580`).

Output: image family `vllm-prod` in `prod-apps-454414`, consumed by
apps/ai/vllm.tf. Cuts cold boot from ~13 min (dnf installs + docker pull
on every launch) to ~2 min (only model download + vLLM warmup).

The model weights (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ) are intentionally not baked
in — they download to /var/lib/vllm/cache on first boot and persist
across restarts, keeping the image small and model swaps cheap.

Build requires VPN connectivity (VM has no external IP; Packer connects
via internal IP). Image is created in us-east1 to satisfy
constraints/gcp.resourceLocations.

Run:
  cd packer/vllm && packer init . && packer build vllm.pkr.hcl

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -5
